sources.name: Stitch - A guide to South African payment rails
Standard Bank Business Online Operational Regulations
World Bank Fast Payments - Real-Time Clearing (RTC) South Africa

entries.subject: payshap_participant_count
entries.display: PayShap has 11 participating banks, not the whole market
entries.quote: There are currently 11 South African banks participating in RPP
entries.notes: Banks named in the same sentence are ABSA, Al Baraka Bank, African Bank, Capitec, Discovery Bank, FNB, HBZ Bank Limited, Investec, Nedbank, OM Bank, Standard Bank and GoTyme Bank (12 names against a stated count of 11). Banks outside this list cannot receive PayShap.

entries.subject: payshap_coverage_incomplete
entries.display: Not every South African bank participates in PayShap
entries.quote: PayShap is available at participating banks, with more banks coming on board soon.
entries.notes: The scheme's own site confirms participation is partial and still expanding. Source page undated; effective date recorded as the 2026-11-02 capture date. [normalised: categorical answer, grade with quote]

entries.subject: payshap_request_first_cohort
entries.display: PayShap Request launched with eight banks in the first cohort
entries.quote: Banks participating in the first cohort include African Bank, Capitec, Discovery Bank, FNB, Investec, Nedbank, Standard Bank and TymeBank, with other banks expected to follow.
entries.notes: Shows PayShap Request initially covered fewer banks than PayShap instant payments.

entries.subject: rtc_participant_coverage
entries.display: RTC participation is a subset of banks; not every bank is a participant
entries.quote: The following banks are participating in RTC
entries.notes: 2017 list: ABSA, African Bank, Bidvest, Capitec, Finbond, FNB, Investec, Nedbank, SASFIN, Standard Bank, U Bank, VBS Mutual. Bidvest and U Bank are acquiring-only.

entries.subject: rtc_clearing_time
entries.display: RTC clears interbank payments within 60 seconds
entries.quote: Allows for clearing of interbank payments within 60 seconds
entries.notes: Corroborated by Standard Bank's operational regulations ('should ideally be cleared within 60 (sixty) seconds') and Stitch. Source page undated; effective date recorded as the 2026-11-02 capture date.

entries.subject: rtc_availability
entries.quote: Uninterrupted access to real-time clearing for your customers (24/7, 365 days a year).
entries.notes: BankServ service features. Source page undated; effective date recorded as the 2026-11-02 capture date.

entries.subject: rtc_annual_volume
entries.notes: World Bank Fast Payments country page for South Africa (2025 data block).

entries.subject: eft_reach
entries.display: EFT moves money between bank accounts and reaches any bank account in South Africa
entries.quote: Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) is the underlying payment rail that moves money between bank accounts in South Africa.

entries.subject: eft_finality
entries.display: A cleared EFT payment is final and irrevocable
entries.quote: It is important to note that once an EFT payment clears, it is final and irrevocable.
entries.notes: Industry explainer. [normalised: categorical answer, grade with quote]

entries.subject: rtgs_operated_by_sarb
entries.display: RTGS handles payments above R5 million and is operated by the SARB
entries.quote: Real-Time Gross Settlements (RTGS) are used for transactions that are higher value than those sent via RTC (i.e. higher value transactions above R5 million), and that require individual settlements.
entries.notes: Corroborated by Standard Bank's rule that items above R5 million must be processed via RTGS. Source page undated; effective date recorded as the 2026-11-02 capture date.

entries.subject: pch_clearing_structure
entries.display: Clearing between banks runs through Payment Clearing Houses governed by PCH agreements
entries.quote: The specific transaction types and applicable Clearing Rules relevant to each PCH are agreed upon amongst members forming part of a Participant Group (PG), which would be responsible for one or more PCH agreements.
entries.notes: Explains why interoperability is rule-bound per payment stream rather than universal. Source page undated; effective date recorded as the 2026-11-02 capture date.

notes: Coverage is recorded as partial: PayShap lists participating banks only, and RTC participation is a subset of banks. Timings come from BankServAfrica and Standard Bank; volumes from the World Bank Fast Payments page.
